title: History timeline: camera along the axis (9:16)
description: A 30-second vertical history explainer: the title rises and slides into a header while a timeline axis draws itself; the camera glides along the axis to five events, one year each, as year ticks and a ghost year counter roll by; at each one a pin drops with a ripple and a card lands with the date, a headline and a one-line note; the travelled axis lights and a progress track fills; the camera zooms out to every pin with its date and a summary line. Code-rendered (scene.history-timeline) with a procedural ambient pad, a whoosh on every camera move, a click on every pin and a swell into the summary.

copy_examples.brief: A short history of the bicycle for a cycling club's channel: in 1817 Karl Drais rode his running machine with no pedals; in 1861 Pierre Michaux added pedals to the front wheel; in 1871 the high-wheel penny-farthing arrived; in 1885 John Kemp Starley's Rover safety bicycle brought the chain-driven rear wheel; in 1888 John Boyd Dunlop patented the pneumatic tyre. Point: the bike we ride today was settled by 1890.

copy_examples.note: Years are the numbers the brief states; names keep the brief's spelling; each note is one detail the brief gives, and the summary restates its point without new facts.

style.typography: Inter, heavy title and dates, bold headlines, medium notes

direction.action: Title into header and the axis draws; the camera travels to five events in order, each pin lands and its card follows; the camera zooms out to every pin and the summary

notes: The animation is code (recipes/scene/history-timeline) rendered frame-exactly on a virtual clock; the content model supplies copy and a look.

Years are VERBATIM numbers: a writer may only use a number the brief states, never compute, round or invent one; a brief without a year for an event ends incomplete. The template takes whole AD years; richer dates ('July 1969', 'c. 3000 BCE') need the recipe directly. Event headlines are written but must keep names exactly as the brief spells them.
Copy is fitted with measured glyphs: dates, headlines and notes each share one size across all cards, and the recipe throws rather than overflow (headlines max 34 characters, notes 52, summary 72).

At 30 s the camera moves into each event over 1.0 s and the pins land at 2.3, 7.1, 11.9, 16.7, 21.5 s (clicks; whooshes peak mid-move); the zoom-out starts at 26.4 s and the summary lands at 27.0 s (swell peak), derived from the recipe's intro, beat and outro formulas.

When every date contains a year, the ticks and the ghost counter follow those years; even spacing is locked, so distances between pins are not to scale (the rolling counter shows the years in between).

quality_gates.description: Integrated loudness lands within 1 LU of the -14 LUFS delivery target.
Decoded true peak stays at or below -0.5 dBTP after AAC encoding.
No stretch of blank picture (no visible contrast, any colour) lasts longer than 0.5 seconds.
A reviewer checks every date and headline against a cited source and confirms the events are in chronological order.
A reviewer confirms the notes and summary add no claim, number or name the brief and its sources do not support.
